description: Reads the registrant list of one webinar: name, email, signup time, attended, watched replay, purchased, UTM source, and what each registrant spent. Read-only, it changes nothing. Data comes only from the WordPress site this chat is connected to, the site the host approved, never from another site. Personal data is returned only when the host's licence includes the registrant export (export_leads). Without that licence the site answers with the code license_required and no personal data, plus a plain explanation of which plan includes the feature. Use it when the host asks who registered, how many leads came in, whom to follow up, or what a single lead bought. Do not use it for aggregate numbers (that is wi_get_webinar_funnel_conversion_stats), for deleting data or for exporting a file. With `all_webinars: true` it reads the registrants of every webinar in one answer, in the order of the webinar list, with `took_ms` and `complete`; that is the way to ask for all of them, not one call per webinar. Without a connected site the answer carries example numbers marked sample: true, from a static demo file that contains no real person.

all_webinars.description: Read every webinar of the site in one answer instead of one webinar. Ignored when webinar_id is given.

limit.description: How many registrants to return per webinar, 1-200. Default 50. The site caps at 200 per call and has no offset, so a longer list is only reachable in parts.

session_id.description: From an earlier turn (weiter · texte · stand).

site.description: Which connected site is meant when this chat has more than one: the address exactly as wi_get_connector_status lists it under sites. Leave it out while only one site is connected.

webinar_id.description: The webinar (campaign) id. Leave it out when the session already built one.

name: wi_list_webinar_leads_registrants
title: List webinar registrants and leads
